raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in the 7th Arrondissement.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"When you're ready, head for Les Invalides — about a 55-minute walk from here.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It began with a king who couldn't stand what he saw.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Louis XIV kept passing war cripples begging on the Pont-Neuf, men who'd given loyal service on the battlefield, and the Sun King decided he owed them a respectable roof.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"So in 1670, with his minister Louvois, he founded the Hôtel des Invalides.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"He wasn't the first to try — Henri IV had sheltered veterans back in 1604 on what's now the rue Broca, and Louis XIII and Richelieu built the hospital of Bicêtre.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But Louis XIV thought big, commissioning Libéral Bruant for something colossal yet oddly subdued in character.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look up as you come to it.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The façade runs 195 metres across, and the main courtyard, the Cour d'Honneur, measures 102 metres by 63.","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Montesquieu called it 'the most respectable place on earth.'","source_id":"b7a472fe-63b8-4c69-8f14-3e309a6a71e7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Take a moment to take it in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Down in the crypt of Saint-Louis-des-Invalides lies Rouget de Lisle, a captain from Strasbourg.","source_id":"8b3acd90-b0b1-4cbd-9d22-e3241c677cb9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1792 he composed 'Le Chant de guerre pour l'armée du Rhin', the song that became La Marseillaise, France's ferociously sanguinary national anthem.","source_id":"8b3acd90-b0b1-4cbd-9d22-e3241c677cb9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His ashes were brought here on 14 July 1915, meant to move on to the Panthéon — a transfer that still hasn't happened.","source_id":"8b3acd90-b0b1-4cbd-9d22-e3241c677cb9","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Then came Napoleon, determined to eclipse his predecessor and stamp the place as his own.","source_id":"f2e93df2-c5cf-42c7-86d1-7399de4e090d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1797 he hauled the lion of the defeated Serenissima Republic to this stronghold of French military glory and set it atop a fountain in the middle of the Esplanade.","source_id":"f2e93df2-c5cf-42c7-86d1-7399de4e090d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"He even hoped to bring back the golden cross of the Kremlin as a trophy for the Dome — but history decided otherwise.","source_id":"f2e93df2-c5cf-42c7-86d1-7399de4e090d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The lion's Paris career was short; by 1815 it was back on its column in Piazza San Marco.","source_id":"f2e93df2-c5cf-42c7-86d1-7399de4e090d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Napoleon wanted to rest 'on the banks of the Seine, by the French people whom I have loved so much.'","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It took seven years of negotiating with the English, but his ashes left Saint Helena and reached Paris on 15 December 1840 — via Le Havre, up the Seine to Pont de Neuilly, then down the Champs-Élysées through a snowstorm.","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Victor Hugo was there when the sun broke through as the hearse appeared: 'The effect was prodigious indeed.'","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Some 850,000 Parisians came to pay homage in the days that followed.","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"His body only reached its permanent tomb, designed by Visconti, on 2 April 1861.","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"He lies inside six nested coffins.","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"A silver vase holds his heart; a silver box, his stomach.","source_id":"cfffad1c-1fa4-4a23-acb2-dadc9332dff8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The dome above you is Jules-Hardouin Mansart's masterpiece — the Royal Chapel, one of the outstanding monuments of 17th-century Paris.","source_id":"e4fad496-62a8-47bf-884d-2d371022d7e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"There was a time you saw it best from Avenue de Breteuil on a fine morning, when the deep purple dome looked almost palpably mellow and pulpy.","source_id":"e4fad496-62a8-47bf-884d-2d371022d7e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Then Paris was groomed for the bicentenary of the Revolution, and the dome was daubed with shiny gold paint.","source_id":"e4fad496-62a8-47bf-884d-2d371022d7e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The regilding was flawless, but it destroyed what only time can bestow.","source_id":"e4fad496-62a8-47bf-884d-2d371022d7e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"By night, though, shimmering against the dark sky above the floodlit walls, it's still enchanting.","source_id":"e4fad496-62a8-47bf-884d-2d371022d7e8","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Remember Louvois, who helped found all this? He fancied the Invalides for his own sepulchre.","source_id":"0ef1619a-ec95-466e-8de6-525bcc99c05f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Louis XIV wouldn't tolerate the impertinence and had his remains removed elsewhere.","source_id":"0ef1619a-ec95-466e-8de6-525bcc99c05f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But Louvois found a subtler way to keep his name here.","source_id":"0ef1619a-ec95-466e-8de6-525bcc99c05f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"As you step into the Cour d'Honneur, look at the fifth garret to the right of the left-hand pavilion — its bull's-eye window is framed by a wolf, a 'loup', that gazes, 'voit', intently down on the courtyard.","source_id":"0ef1619a-ec95-466e-8de6-525bcc99c05f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"A far-fetched pun, and one that slipped right past the Sun King.","source_id":"0ef1619a-ec95-466e-8de6-525bcc99c05f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One last thing, in the institution's original church — Saint-Louis-des-Invalides, also designed by Bruant and home to a magnificent 17th-century organ.","source_id":"004e0c2d-a67e-47be-88f6-e02618786cac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Here, on 5 December 1837, Hector Berlioz's Requiem had its world premiere — 188 instrumentalists and 210 choristers, at a ceremony for General Damrémont, killed at the Siege of Constantine.","source_id":"004e0c2d-a67e-47be-88f6-e02618786cac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0}]}
